name: Mandy, Indiana
label: Sacred Bones
lede: A Manchester band that began as Gary, Indiana, recorded a debut in a cave and a crypt, and got its best reviews yet for an album with billy woods on it.

eras.title: A gig in Manchester, a name from Gary
eras.text: Scott Fair and Valentine Caulfield meet through the city's DIY circuit, add a drummer, and are on Brooklyn's Fire Talk by the end of 2020.

years.cap: Scott Fair and Valentine Caulfield, the band's founding pair.
years.src: Beats Per Minute · Loud And Quiet · Wikipedia: Mandy, Indiana
years.h: A guitarist watches a French singer in Melk and asks her to start something
years.p: [[Scott Fair|e9b33f29-295a-4c56-8a84-67640c72c727]] saw [[Valentine Caulfield|43136653-0461-4f61-8dcc-fee474051012]] play in a band called Melk and noticed she sounded like nothing else on the Manchester circuit. They called themselves Gary, Indiana.
years.xp:
Fair told Beats Per Minute that Caulfield's performance with Melk "wasn't really like anything else I'd seen in the local music circuit." The two stayed in touch on social media after both their bands supported the Newcastle act Mouses, then started writing together. Caulfield, who grew up in Paris and sings mostly in French, has said the working relationship ran about three years before the band was properly a band.

Loud And Quiet reported that Fair had been looking for a female vocalist who could speak French. Liam Stewart, a touring drummer for [[Lonelady|d2b5dd20-6172-4bba-a668-8fc2e8113939]], completed the trio after Fair met him through a party connection. Wikipedia gives 2018 as the start; other write-ups say 2016 or 2017, so treat the year as approximate.

years.src: Circuit Sweet · Fire Talk: Mandy, Indiana EPK
years.p: Before any label, the trio put out "Berlin" and "Pashto" themselves, with Stewart on percussion.
years.xp: Fire Talk's bio and Circuit Sweet both list the two self-released singles as the band's first music, ahead of the label deal. The pitch was already set: French-language vocals, heavy drums and electronics, with film directors Gaspar Noé and Leos Carax named as touchstones.

years.h: Fire Talk signs them with "Nike of Samothrace"
years.p: The Brooklyn label announced the deal with a single, directed by Will Shields, that the band wanted to hit "like a blunt instrument."
years.xp: The band told press the track had "all dials turned up full," drawing on film scores and experimental percussion. It was the first release on Fire Talk, the New York label that would put out everything up to the debut album.

eras.title: Fourth member, five tracks
eras.text: A synth player arrives, the name changes to Mandy, Indiana, and the ...EP turns them from a trio into a band people write about.

years.src: Stereogum: Album of the Week · Wikipedia: Mandy, Indiana · Paste: Mandy, Indiana Dance Through the Fury
years.p: The name honored the Indiana steel town that gave the world the Jacksons and Freddie Gibbs. The "Mandy" version came later.
years.xp: Stereogum notes the original name paid homage to Gary, the industrial city outside Chicago. Wikipedia says the band switched to Mandy on the record label's advice; Fair told Paste the change came from workshopping names until "Mandy" had the right rhythm. The date is not pinned down in the sources, but the 2021 single "Alien 3" is already filed under both names on Fire Talk's site.

years.src: Paste: Mandy, Indiana Dance Through the Fury · Crack Magazine
years.h: Simon Catling joins on synth, a drummer swap follows
years.p: [[Simon Catling|45ca79ad-3e96-4bb0-a42b-684609fcc6f1]], who once threw Caulfield out of a club, becomes the fourth member; [[Alex Macdougall|4257bc0f-c6a7-4a6b-862c-7d13c2d0fe4e]] later replaces Stewart on drums.
years.xp: Fair told Paste that Catling first met Caulfield when "he was throwing her out of a club he was working at." Crack reported Catling joined in summer 2021 and Macdougall took over after Stewart left. Stewart still plays on the ...EP, so the drummer change came after it.

years.p: The Fire Talk EP collects "Bottle Episode," "Nike of Samothrace" and "Alien 3" with remixes by [[Daniel Avery|3e7aa4a4-5b7e-46a3-a7ff-c57044fa1b64]] and Club Eat.
years.xp: The EP runs 24 minutes 56 seconds and was produced by Fair. Pitchfork's Max Freedman gave it 7.6 and said it walks "a fine line between violent and groovy." The name is three dots, on purpose: DIY described it as deliberately un-Google-friendly.

eras.title: Caves, a crypt, a mall
eras.text: The debut is recorded on location, lands Best New Music, and takes them to Texas and the US.

years.cap: Recording on location for i've seen a way.
q: We're trying to rattle people's bones, really.
years.src: MusicRadar · Uproxx · Wikipedia: I've Seen a Way · Treble
years.h: They haul a drum kit into Wookey Hole Caves and press record
years.p: The debut was recorded in a Somerset cave, a Bristol crypt, a Leeds nave, a Manchester club and a shopping mall. A cave diver interrupted one take.
years.xp:
MusicRadar's account: a 20 minute walk to the site, water dripping onto a Tascam desk and a full kit, and no way to monitor the sound because it was too loud. The way out led past a cheese-maturing facility and a 50ft King Kong statue. Fair called it the hardest day of recording he's had.

The crypt at The Mount Without in Bristol gave short, hard reflections; the band's noise disturbed a meditation and yoga group in the church above. Caulfield found the mall's reverb on a walk, and her phone recordings ended up in a track.

years.h: "Injury Detail" is the first new music since the EP
years.p: Made with Fair and [[Robin Stewart|156d6128-e4f0-4c74-b14a-c35bab0cdb80]] of [[Giant Swan|bcd1d1f5-140c-445a-b139-46d31be6a2a8]], it opens on organ and turns into a warehouse dance track. Thomas Harrington Rawle directed the video.
years.xp: Caulfield said the song came from feeling trapped in a liminal space, with guitars making the landscape feel limitless. Fire Talk also announced the band's US debut at SXSW 2023.

years.src: Wikipedia: I've Seen a Way · DIY
yt: Pinking Shears, live at Green Man
years.h: i've seen a way gets Pitchfork's Best New Music
years.p: Pitchfork's Ryan Leas gave the Fire Talk debut an 8.3 and called it purposefully disorienting. Fair produced.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, the album carries a Metacritic weighted average of 79 across nine reviews. Leas wrote that it blurs genres and defamiliarizes language. Caulfield told DIY the aim was always something that didn't sound like anything else, and that the day they make an expected album is the day the band is dead.

years.p: She moved from Manchester, citing rising costs and the city's disappearing identity, per NME. The band now works between the two cities.

years.src: Uproxx · Wikipedia: I've Seen a Way · NME
years.p: The band played Los Angeles, San Francisco and Brooklyn, and the debut finished 20th on Pitchfork's 2023 list, 44th at the Guardian and 46th at Stereogum.
years.xp: The rankings are as reported on Wikipedia's page for the album. NME also reported the band had opened for IDLES, Gilla Band and Squid, and played SXSW in Austin.

eras.title: Sacred Bones and URGH
eras.text: A label move, a Gilla Band co-producer and a billy woods guest verse produce the year's best-reviewed noise record.

years.src: BrooklynVegan · The Line of Best Fit · Paste: Mandy, Indiana URGH Album Review
years.h: They sign to Sacred Bones and announce URGH with "Magazine"
years.p: The Brooklyn label announces a February 6 release, co-produced by Scott Fair and Daniel Fox of Gilla Band, with all four members writing.
years.xp: Caulfield described "Magazine" as expressing "the frustration and deep-seated violence I felt while attempting to recover from being raped," and said she wrote it as a way to confront her attacker. Paste noted the track builds from light percussion into explosive chaos.

q: I feel like I'm not very good at telling when I need to rest.
years.src: Wikipedia: Urgh · Stereogum: Album of the Week · Exclaim! · The Creative Independent
years.p: Pitchfork's Walden Green scored the second album 8.5, praising its blend of industrial, post-punk and 80s neo-noir soundtrack.
years.xp:
Recorded at Greenmount in Leeds, Airtight in Manchester and Flow in Berlin, and mixed with Fox. Metacritic lists an 85 for universal acclaim; Stereogum named it Album of the Week on February 3. Exclaim! called it "the first great album of 2026." Wikipedia lists it at number 1 on the UK Dance Albums chart.

The making was hard on the body. Caulfield had multiple surgeries and Macdougall a hernia and thyroid issues during the sessions. He told The Creative Independent he finished the drum takes two months after surgery.

years.src: Stereogum: Mandy, Indiana Team With billy woods · Exclaim!
years.h: "Sicko!" puts billy woods over broken industrial techno
years.p: The rapper from [[Armand Hammer|167a6f86-2c26-43fe-82f0-e4c8a39ea490]] guests. The band hired seven filmmakers to make 30-second clips for it, instead of one video.
years.xp: The band said they wanted to work with someone who had inspired them, and called woods "such a unique voice in hip hop." Exclaim! read the song as addressing healthcare and pharmaceutical exploitation.

years.h: UK and Europe tour: London, Paris, Berlin, Amsterdam
years.p: The spring run of dates, announced with the album, was set to run from late March into mid-April.
